candidate_relations.rationale: The package-builder tests show only allowlisted roots enter the manifest, project-owned material is excluded, and unsafe symlinks fail closed, strengthening the package-build configuration boundary.
Byte-identical clean builds, allowlisted manifest contents, project-owned exclusion, and symlink rejection strengthen the deterministic release-package builder proposition.

The bootstrap tests show explicit identity creates project/2 and legacy migration requires explicit identity, strengthening the runtime requirement that v2 identity fields be explicit rather than repository-derived.
The bootstrap runtime permits v2 migration only from an explicit complete identity, strengthening the v2 requirement for exactly the non-empty explicit identity fields rather than inferred values.

The ingestion operation creates request and activation artifacts without model execution or Canon mutation and bounds its evidence selection, strengthening the production-invocation boundary that Distiller has no reconciliation or admission authority.

The Phase 0 rule preserving raw candidates separately from evaluation diagnostics strengthens the production-invocation prohibition on post-model semantic repair or normalization of raw candidate bytes.

The production-invocation tests verify exact raw candidate bytes are preserved without post-hoc repair, strengthening the Phase 0 baseline requirement for raw candidate preservation separate from diagnostics.
The production contract explicitly requires unchanged raw candidate bytes and prohibits semantic repair, strengthening the earlier raw-candidate preservation boundary.

The workflow tests verify immutable definition identity binds intent and authentication and that competing normative transitions fail stale-head checks, strengthening the workflow contract’s immutable bounded-intent model.

The workflow tests show auto-advance requires explicit prospective confirmation and extension events do not silently advance normative state, strengthening the rule that workflow intent itself grants no downstream authority.

The grant tests show bounded approval consumption, revocation semantics, and exact-head issuance, strengthening the grant-operations proposition that grant authority is constrained rather than a generic mutation path.

The grant tests exercise issuance-time consumption, revocation, and exact-head concurrency, strengthening the common mutation substrate’s treatment of grant-derived approvals as exact immutable approval evidence.
Deterministic candidate-submission identity from invocation and canonical graph bytes strengthens the production test proposition that valid fixed evidence produces an immutable candidate submission.

The migration requirement to preserve project-owned knowledge and authority while replacing runtime coupling strengthens the install-package rule that updates must not silently migrate canonical project knowledge.
The operator-management tests verify root transfer requires current-root approval, exact confirmation, and one protected root after success, strengthening the protected-root transfer contract.

The architecture rule that append-only histories are authoritative and projections create no authority independently strengthens the operator-registry model of authoritative events and a deterministic current projection.
Limiting grant-derived approval issuance to the exact proposal covered by a grant strengthens the common-mutation invariant that grant-derived approval remains bound to one immutable proposal.

The RGP Submission Protocol keeps candidate production, reconciliation, admission, and canonical persistence distinct, strengthening the orchestrator contract’s requirement that consuming projects not reinterpret or collapse package-owned normative protocol boundaries.

The provenance contract’s explicit non-authority rule strengthens the governance runtime’s typed operational-provenance representation by clarifying that such references carry observational context rather than authority.
